Based on this scriptural passage, there would then be a place for riding donkeys. The answer is: no.
Later generations built a terrace upon it and planted trees as an offering;
how could a donkey ever have been stationed beside a Buddha hall?
Furthermore, the name "Middle Donkey" (Zhonglu) was originally the site of the ancient territory of the state of Lü.
Later generations have lacked practice and thus have made various groundless conjectures regarding this matter.
This one-fascicle work, *Gantong lu* (Records of Miraculous Responses), was compiled by Vinaya Master Daoxuan.
It is not found in the Tibetan canon;
however, Ke Hong’s *Shu* (Commentary) states that it was discovered during the collation of scriptures according to the *Zhenyuan lu*.
The Elder Eitō transmitted this and sent it bound in a volume;
therefore, it is contained herein.
